name: cursor-pagination
title: Cursor pagination
description: Older and Newer for feeds and APIs that page by cursor: no page numbers, no total, a spinner that keeps the button's width and a plain end state.
docs: Pass hasPrevious and hasNext from your API (a cursor, a next-page token, a Link header) and handle onPrevious and onNext; previous is the newer page and next the older one. loading is 'previous', 'next' or false and says which way a request is in flight: that button shows a spinner in place of its arrow, so it keeps its width, and is marked aria-busy, while the other one waits, dimmed. Neither is disabled, so a keyboard user keeps their place and a second press does nothing. When there is nothing further the button is replaced by plain text, 'No newer results' at the start of the list and 'No older results' at the end, instead of a dead control. range is your own text ('21 to 40') in a polite live region, so a screen reader hears where it landed after each step; at an end of the list the same region also says so ('16 to 20. No older results.'). The range is empty until you give it one. When the button that was used with the keyboard (or a click that focused it) is replaced by its end text, focus moves onto the text, so a keyboard user is not thrown out of the list; if the reader has moved on by then, focus is left alone. hrefs ({ previous, next }) makes the buttons real links, for pages a crawler can follow and a reader can open in a new tab; with a handler as well, a plain click goes to the handler and a middle or modified click opens the address. With links and no handlers it can be rendered from a Server Component (a page.tsx): the component is a client component, so only data goes in, and the links are in the HTML. labels holds the four texts for another language. In a container narrower than 24rem the range moves above the two buttons.
